amendment_1.classification: root and coordinator scoped; recorded as a covariate, not a treatment change
amendment_1.reasoning: The treatment under test is worker-facing read-set sizing. No line this commit changes is worker-facing in effect, and the measured worker read set grows by 1110 bytes of root-only material, roughly 280 tokens. Reverting would withdraw a root-transfer capability to protect an experiment of about n=3 builders per slice from a change that cannot touch the measured path.
amendment_1.bias_direction: against H1. The worker read set is 1110 bytes larger, so context at first code write is pushed up, not down. The change cannot manufacture support for H1; if H1 is supported, it is supported against this small headwind.

residual_defect.what: anthropic-host.md, a worker-read file, now carries a root-transfer section that workers cannot execute.
residual_defect.consequence: about 280 tokens of every worker's startup reading is a procedure for a role it does not hold, in a skill whose own change under test tells workers to read only what their packet names.
residual_defect.remedy: move the root-specific section out of the worker read set
residual_defect.deferred: applying that move would change the measured text; it should wait until R2 finishes

Such a change pauses R2 or voids the comparison with B1-B6, and must be declared before dispatch.
standing_rule_for_further_skill_changes.covariate: changes confined to root, coordinator or supervisor procedure. Recorded with commit, per-file byte delta inside the worker read set, and bias direction.
standing_rule_for_further_skill_changes.applies_to: the unapplied v2 skill diff as well; classify it by this rule before applying it, and prefer holding it until R2 finishes

amendment_2.trigger: the orchestration side reported R2's subject is a controller and projector of 369 JavaScript lines against a criterion of two Rust slices of 2000-5000 lines
amendment_2.finding: 369 JavaScript lines cannot test R2 as registered, and the criterion as written named the wrong quantity.

why_the_subject_fails.H1: the baseline 94,353 came from builders reading a 2,700-line Rust crate plus contract sections. A far smaller read set lowers context at first code write for a reason the hypothesis does not claim, so the result would be uninterpretable.
why_the_subject_fails.H2: the failure mode, a builder consuming its context without writing, occurs under a large read set. With a small one, 0 of n is the expected result whatever the instruction says.
why_the_subject_fails.H3: handoffs arise from context pressure; small slices do not generate it.
why_the_subject_fails.H4: needs a comparable Rust denominator against B4. 369 JavaScript lines is not one.

criterion_restated.was: at least two Rust-building slices of 2000-5000 added Rust lines each
criterion_restated.now: each scored code slice must give its builders a read set of at least 2000 existing lines, and add at least 1000 lines in one language; at least 3 code-slice builders in total
criterion_restated.why: the causal driver of B1, B2 and B3 is the size of the read set a builder is given, not the size of its output. The original criterion named the output and so would have excluded a qualifying experiment and admitted a non-qualifying one.
criterion_restated.H4_condition: H4 is scored only if the added lines are Rust. Otherwise H4 is recorded as not established, and H1-H3 can still be scored.
criterion_restated.honesty_note: this is a change to acceptance criteria made after learning that the intended subject does not fit, and before any R2 data exists. It is stated as an amendment rather than presented as the original criterion.

amendment_2.ruling: If the scout finds no slice meeting the restated criterion, do not bend the registration to fit the subject. Run the port as a delivery campaign, instrumented identically, recorded as an observational cohort labelled not-R2, and leave R2 frozen and pending. Several small observational campaigns can be pooled later; one bent registration cannot be unbent.
instrumentation_requested_even_if_not_sc: per-builder context at first code write
the read set each packet names, and how many existing lines it comprises
context checks at each phase boundary
handoffs per slice, with declaration reading and turnaround

amendment_3.title: Two of seven B1 values were detector false positives; B1 and B6 corrected
amendment_3.wrong_claim: B1 context at first code write: median 94,353, mean 89,846, range 58,097-116,779 (n=6), and B6 median 15, range 10-29 (n=7).
amendment_3.error_class: instrument defect: the first-code-write detector accepted any Bash command containing both a '>' character and the substring '.rs', so a redirect to an unrelated path (2>/dev/null, > /tmp/x, > a .md result file) in a command that merely mentioned a .rs path counted as a code write. It also counted a Cargo.toml write as a code write.

a27d1ec9c1e4acca4.reason: 88,562 was the first write of Cargo.toml (cat > ... Cargo.toml, call 24). The first write of a .rs file is at call 28.

a74b04b4ca3160232.reason: 58,097 was a write of /tmp/x and a mutate.py under the run directory (call 15), not crate source. The first .rs write is a heredoc Python patch of tests/rederive.rs at call 38.

amendment_3.downstream_consequence: H1's bar was set 7,696 tokens below the true pre-change median, which made H1 harder to support than the data warrants. Correcting it moves the bar in the direction that favours the treatment. B2 (1 of 7) and B3-B5 are unaffected: B2's instance was re-verified as having no write candidate of any kind, and B3-B5 do not use this detector.
amendment_3.check_that_caught_it: Instrumenting the P1 builder, the detector reported a first code write on a command that was a sed/cat read with 2>/dev/null in it. Re-running with a write-construct regex then disagreed with the frozen table on two builders, and each of the seven was adjudicated by listing every candidate write call and reading the matched command rather than trusting any detector.
amendment_3.sequence_disclosure: This amendment was made while the P1 builder was running and after its first code write had been measured. At the time of amendment P1's first .rs write was 81,055 with 26 pre-write read calls. P1 is an observational cohort labelled not R2 and is not scored against B1 as an R2 result; the disclosure is recorded so the order of discovery is auditable.
amendment_3.second_defect_found_and_fixed: The replacement detector's own git-commit test matched only the literal 'git commit' and so missed 'git -C <dir> commit'. Both detector versions are therefore unreliable on their own; the committed values come from read adjudication of every candidate.

amendment_5.classification_basis: amendment 1's standing rule: changes confined to root, coordinator or supervisor procedure

amendment_5.worker_facing_adoption: deferred until R2 ends; stated in the skill's own first paragraph. Referencing it from a worker packet, a shared instruction or inherited context would make it treatment-relevant and pause R2 or void the B1-B6 comparison. Verified per dispatch, not once
amendment_5.bias_rationale: zero worker-text delta does not imply zero experimental effect: root-side coordination can change dispatch order, packet content, how early a scope collision is caught and how often a worker is corrected mid-run, hence cost, handoffs and outcomes. amendment_5.what_would_settle_it: R2 slices dispatched with and without root-side channel use; this campaign is not sized to provide that. Until then it is a named uncertainty in R2's limits, not a quantified adjustment
